growth_signal.value: Over $70M in bookings in 2024, more than 25 million tickets sold, 150+ operators in four countries; launched corporate travel in 2026

raised.value: about $2.9M over four rounds, plus an undisclosed 2025 investment from Yango Ventures

entry.idea: Sells bus, train and flight tickets across East Africa from a phone, even a basic one without internet, and gives the bus companies software to run their business.
entry.lesson: Digitise the suppliers first and the marketplace follows; the software for the bus companies is what makes the tickets stick.
entry.name: BuuPass

growth.reason: Big cumulative numbers and steady new operators, but no recent growth rate published.

market.reason: Hundreds of millions of Africans travel by bus, but tickets are cheap and the business is regional for now.

tech.reason: A booking marketplace plus operator software; the USSD access for basic phones is smart but easy to copy.

sources.title: BuuPass taps SafariBucks for cross-border travel payments (TechCabal)
BuuPass secures investment from Yango Ventures (TechCabal)

entry.twist: The bus operators get free back-office software, so the ticket marketplace fills itself with inventory nobody else has digitised.
entry.who_pays: Travellers pay a booking fee; operators pay for the software and premium tools; companies pay for the new corporate travel service.
entry.why_now: Africa's intercity travel still runs on cash and paper, while nearly everyone now carries a phone that can pay.

mentions.snippet: Bus and travel booking across African markets, now with cross-border payments via SafariBucks.

Founded 2017 by Sonia Kabra and Wyclife Omondi; bus, train and flight tickets via web, app and USSD plus software for bus operators; $70M+ bookings in 2024; 25M+ tickets sold; 150+ operators in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, South Africa; $2.94M raised over four rounds
